explanation: Controlled offline reference test passed twice (exit 0, ~0.4 s each). The unchanged analysis built the LuxC profile HMM (NSEQ 13, LENG 400, ACC PF05893.5) from the Stockholm alignment, searched the 12-protein LuxC.faa database via pipeline.search_hmm, printed the first-hit domain alignment (tr|B6ESM7 match), and produced both declared artifacts in /work/outputs: LuxC.hmm (187,150 bytes) and LuxC.domtbl (4,093 bytes, 12 domain rows in hmmsearch domains format). Staged inputs rebuilt byte-identically on both tests (LuxC.sto sha256 e2cf20e9c154..., LuxC.faa sha256 7ce47aaed2c5...). After inspecting the installed pyhmmer test-data assets against the actual produced outputs, two answer-bearing fixtures were declared for removal — the packaged test LuxC.hmm profile (same model parameters; only DATE/version/COM stamp lines differ from the produced HMM) and the LuxC.hmmalign.sto alignment fixture (the printed alignment result) — and the reference was re-run with those removals applied and passed identically. Note: luxC.hmm byte hashes vary between runs only because the writer emits a DATE timestamp and COM command line; all scientific parameter fields (CKSUM 395769323, EFFN 1.989990, NSEQ 13, LENG 400) are reproducible and matched the packaged upstream fixture.
source_adaptations: analysis.py: changed the two input path literals from the notebook-relative "data/msa/LuxC.sto" and "data/seqs/LuxC.faa" to "/inputs/data/msa/LuxC.sto" and "/inputs/data/seqs/LuxC.faa" so the unchanged script finds its staged inputs offline; no other changes — imports, bindings, computation and comments are untouched.

stage-inputs.sh: downloads the two original data files from the pinned source revision raw.githubusercontent.com/althonos/pyhmmer/90d2f28303d9fe795c4e1ffc1e05b9d634319b51/src/pyhmmer/tests/data/{msa/LuxC.sto,seqs/LuxC.faa} (the exact bytes the notebook's data/ paths refer to in the source repository) with SHA-256 verification against e2cf20e9c154... and 7ce47aaed2c5..., staging them under /inputs/data/. No caches or extra lookup metadata are needed: MSAFile/SequenceFile load the files directly in offline mode.
unresolved_assumptions: pyhmmer==0.12.3 was chosen because it is the exact version of the source revision itself and provides cp313 manylinux wheels on this Python 3.13.13 base; the source pins no version, so HMMER-code behavioral details (e.g. output header stamp "3.4 | Aug 2023") follow from that choice.
The exported HMM and domtbl contain runtime DATE stamps and a COM line, so their exact bytes are not stable across executions; the model parameters and scores are reproducible.

Data redistribution terms for the LuxC alignment/sequences (derived from Pfam/InterPro PF05893 and UniProt entries) were not independently reviewed; staging stays limited to the two data files the notebook reads.
